sources.title: The Many Lives of Moses Hadas
sources.locator: Fall 2001; opening biographical section and 'Living many lives' section
sources.rights_notes: Institutional biographical article by Hadas's daughter. Only a short supporting excerpt and project-authored paraphrase are retained.

aliases: Columbia University in the City of New York
organizations.normalization_notes: The institutional source describes Hadas's career in Columbia's Department of Classics and undergraduate teaching at Columbia College.

affiliations.date_precision: The institutional article places the beginning of Hadas's long Columbia classics career in the 1930s and explicitly sequences professor, OSS service, then professor again; it does not supply exact employment transition dates.
affiliations.research_notes: Columbia's article explicitly describes a professor-to-OSS-to-professor sequence. The personnel file is still needed for exact leave, recruitment, and return dates.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Moses Hadas is the Columbia classicist whom Columbia's institutional biography identifies as serving in the OSS during World War II.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive index name is independently linked by Columbia to both a long classics faculty career and OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name and explicit institutional OSS linkage; the index row itself lacks a rank or private identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: Columbia places the academic career before and after OSS service, but the personnel file is required for exact dates.
claims.match_notes: Box 302 remains the direct personnel-file confirmation path.

claims.claim_text: Moses Hadas was a Columbia University classics professor immediately before his OSS service and returned to the Columbia faculty afterward.
claims.evidence_excerpt: a professor; then ... an O.S.S. operative ... and then a professor again
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Columbia's institutional biography gives a direct professor-to-OSS-to-professor sequence and describes his long career in its classics department.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name and explicit OSS service in the employer's own institutional publication.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded immediate civilian affiliation: the article directly sequences his professorship before OSS service and his return afterward, although exact transition dates are absent.
claims.match_notes: Also marked as last civilian employer before service. Do not infer an exact leave date or that his Columbia appointment formally ended.

sources.locator_override: Opening biographical section and Living many lives section

claims.claim_text: Columbia University is the last documented civilian employer before Moses Hadas's OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Columbia account presents no intervening civilian employer between his professorship and OSS service and records his later return to professorial work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name and direct institutional OSS linkage.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded but not day-specific; Box 302 is needed to establish exact administrative dates.
claims.match_notes: This is a last-documented-employer claim, not a claim that his Columbia appointment was terminated during service.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The distinctive exact index name is independently corroborated by a Columbia institutional biography that explicitly describes Moses Hadas as a Columbia professor and OSS operative.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 302 for exact Columbia leave status, OSS recruitment and service dates, and the administrative relationship between the faculty appointment and wartime service.

research_attempts.query_text: Moses Hadas OSS Columbia professor official institutional biography archives
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Wikipedia and derivative biographical summaries were discovery-only; a Columbia finding-aid cross-reference did not itself establish the employment-to-OSS sequence; postwar teaching references were unnecessary.
research_attempts.research_notes: The NARA index and Columbia's employer-published chronology support a high-confidence identity and strongly date-bounded Columbia-to-OSS pathway. Exact administrative dates remain unresolved.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 302 for exact transition dates and appointment status during wartime service.
